name: Mailchimp
tagline: Email marketing platform with campaigns, automations, forms, and analytics

pricing.notes: Official pricing page checked; 2026 public coverage lists Standard starting at $20/month for small contact counts, with subscriber-based scaling and discounts/promos.

verdictSummary: A campaign sender is buildable, but Mailchimp's value is deliverability, templates, compliance, automations, segmentation, ecommerce integrations, and support.
coreLoopDIY: Build subscriber lists, campaign composer, templates, segmentation, sends via SES/Postmark/Mailgun, unsubscribe and analytics.
whyPeopleStillPay: They pay because email is business-critical and deliverability problems are expensive.

priorArt.name: Mautic
priorArt.desc: Open-source marketing automation platform with email campaigns and contact management.

alternatives.name: Brevo Free
alternatives.desc: Campaigns, forms and automation with many contacts but only 300 daily sends.

alternatives.name: EmailOctopus Free
alternatives.desc: A real small-list plan with forms and simple automations; reports expire after thirty days.

alternatives.name: MailPoet Starter
alternatives.desc: Campaigns, forms, analytics and basic automation inside WordPress; the free list stops at 500.

alternatives.name: Mautic
alternatives.desc: The heavyweight open-source replacement for segmentation and automation; it also replaces ease with operations.

alternatives.name: Notifuse
alternatives.desc: A modern visual campaign and automation stack; you own the database and the deliverability chores.

alternatives.name: Plunk
alternatives.desc: Campaigns, transactional mail and workflows together; audience CRM depth is thinner.

alternatives.name: Sender Free
alternatives.desc: Campaigns, forms, analytics and unlimited workflows in a useful free tier; the monkey can retire.

rejectedAlternatives.name: listmonk
rejectedAlternatives.desc: Campaigns and forms are excellent, but the missing automation builder is not a footnote here.

rejectedAlternatives.name: Mailchimp Free
rejectedAlternatives.desc: The free plan now stops at 250 contacts and omits automation flows; the mascot is mostly a signup form.

rejectedAlternatives.name: SendPortal
rejectedAlternatives.desc: A familiar open-source recommendation with no commit since April 2024.

notes: Classic hidden-moat example: the UI can be rebuilt; inbox placement cannot be hand-waved.
prompt:
Build me a small-list email campaign tool to replace Mailchimp. Requirements:

- Node + Express + better-sqlite3 on my VPS. Admin UI bound to localhost/VPN; only
  the subscribe and unsubscribe endpoints are public.
- Contacts with tags and custom fields, CSV import and export, and segments saved
  as filters (has tag X, joined after date, opened last campaign).
- Campaigns written in Markdown, rendered into one clean single-column HTML email
  with mjml, plain-text alternative generated automatically.
- Send through Amazon SES (keys in .env) with throttling and per-recipient status;
  SES bounce and complaint notifications auto-suppress those addresses.
- Compliance baked in: unsubscribe link and postal address in every footer, a
  List-Unsubscribe header, double opt-in on the public signup form.
- Open tracking is a per-campaign toggle, default off. Campaign report shows sent,
  bounced, and unsubscribed counts.
- One SQLite file holds everything; no telemetry, no third-party trackers.
- Out of scope: the drag-and-drop template editor, automation journeys, and
  ecommerce integrations. One good template, sent well.
- README warning: inbox placement is earned, not coded. Document SPF, DKIM, and
  DMARC setup and tell me to warm up sending volume gradually.
